baseline: 1.1.0; M0–M5 implemented with external PP-037/038 acceptance gates

priorities.P0: Next product foundations and release gates
priorities.P2: Later breadth; not part of the first follow-up slice

phases.title: A reader worth spending time in
phases.label: Lecture confortable
phases.subtitle: Typographie, concentration, symboles et équations
phases.gate: A source paragraph, equation and experiment can be followed comfortably by keyboard and at narrow widths.

phases.title: A richer widget language
phases.label: Widgets expressifs
phases.subtitle: Diagrammes, fonctions, géométrie, probabilités, tenseurs
phases.gate: New catalog types have real controls, accessible values and explicit evidence policies.

phases.title: Exploration and useful automatic enrichment
phases.label: Exploration et Meta
phases.subtitle: Vues liées, hypothèses, couverture et corrections
phases.gate: A reader can inspect and refine a grounded, diverse widget plan; real readers evaluate its usefulness.

phases.title: A personal paper workbench
phases.label: Atelier de recherche
phases.subtitle: Notes, recherche locale, export et création de figures
phases.gate: A reader can author, annotate, find and transfer source-linked work without an account or automatic upload.

phases.title: Compatibility and release quality
phases.label: Qualité durable
phases.subtitle: Migrations et performances
phases.gate: Old experiments survive supported upgrades and the richer reader stays responsive.

phases.title: Final Railway release
phases.label: Release Railway
phases.subtitle: À la fin : service, stockage, accès et vérifications
phases.gate: Provision and verify the final Railway Node deployment only when the product is ready for release.

issues.title: Make long-form reading comfortable and configurable
issues.goal: Read a dense section for ten minutes without tiny labels, overlong lines or a dashboard dominating the paper.
issues.scope: Establish an editorial reading system: 18/20/22 px body presets, 55–75 ch measure, line-height 1.55–1.85, paragraph rhythm, clear heading hierarchy and light/sepia/high-contrast themes. Store preferences locally; preserve source text.
acceptanceCriteria: One reading-settings control applies and restores font size, measure, spacing and theme across prepared and imported papers.
The default desktop body is 20 px; essential controls are at least 16 px and auxiliary text at least 14 px, with documented contrast checks.
Text-spacing overrides, 200% zoom, 320 px width, long equations and dark/high-contrast preferences retain readable text and reachable controls.
Changing preferences preserves the current source anchor and does not modify source content or trigger inference.
issues.verification: Inspect paragraph/equation/figure fixtures at desktop and 320 px, zoom and spacing overrides; keyboard-test settings and restoration.
issues.evidencePolicy: presentation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Reduce visual noise with compact figures and progressive controls
issues.goal: Follow the argument continuously while opening the relevant experiment only when needed.
issues.scope: Separate the source, added intuition and experiment controls visually. Use compact inline figures with an optional inspection panel, contextual Ask actions and expandable assumptions/evidence; retain a short visible truth label.
acceptanceCriteria: Original paragraphs no longer each require a permanently visible Ask button; the action is available through keyboard/focus as well as selection.
Inputs, playback, source return and an essential evidence label remain discoverable while advanced settings and long diagnostics are collapsed.
Expanding a widget or opening the inspection panel preserves reading position and supports Escape/focus return.
Desktop and narrow-screen layouts avoid nested scroll traps and preserve accessible reading order.
issues.verification: Compare source-heavy and figure-heavy sections in actual browser use; exercise keyboard-only expansion and screen-width changes.
issues.evidencePolicy: presentation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Add focus reading and source-aware navigation
issues.goal: Move between a concept, its explanation and its experiment without losing the place in the paper.
issues.scope: Provide a focus reading mode, collapsible contents, current-section indication, anchor breadcrumbs and a return-to-reading control. Keep PDF physical pages distinct from HTML logical positions.
acceptanceCriteria: Contents track the visible source section and support keyboard navigation without stealing focus during ordinary scrolling.
Entering and leaving focus mode restores the selected source block, figure and scroll position.
Source citations and figure return links reveal the correct passage even when surrounding sections or panels are collapsed.
Progress is based on disclosed source positions; no invented page number or precise reading-time estimate is shown.
issues.verification: Navigate between distant sections and figures, reload mid-paper, and exercise HTML and PDF sources with stable anchors.
issues.evidencePolicy: presentation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Explain mathematical symbols and terminology in context
issues.goal: Understand a symbol or technical term without opening a separate chat and losing the current paragraph.
issues.scope: Add a source-linked symbol glossary and term popovers, including scope-specific meanings, definitions and prerequisites. Start from authored fixtures; opt-in Meta suggestions remain interpretations.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a symbol or term shows its definition, scope, source reference and whether the definition is authored, quoted or generated.
A symbol reused with two meanings in different sections retains both scoped definitions instead of a single global guess.
Popover access works on focus/keyboard and touch; dismissal returns focus and does not obscure the whole equation.
Missing definitions remain explicitly unresolved; a generated definition cannot replace original source text.
issues.verification: Use repeated symbols, absent definitions, ambiguous terms and citation-jump fixtures; review generated examples against their sources.
issues.evidencePolicy: source-linked interpretation
issues.inferencePolicy: Authored/cached definitions are free; requesting missing Meta definitions is explicit, bounded, quota-accounted and cached per source version.

issues.title: Offer intuition, worked examples and technical explanation layers
issues.goal: Let a student find an entry point while an experienced reader can stay close to the original argument.
issues.scope: Add optional layers per anchored concept: intuition, a small worked example, assumptions and technical detail. Use the same source and a consistent example across layers; do not rewrite the source into simplified prose.
acceptanceCriteria: The original passage remains available and visually distinct in every layer.
A reader can reveal a prerequisite or worked example locally without changing the whole document or issuing another model call.
Worked examples explicitly identify synthetic inputs, assumptions and any actual engine result; unexecuted steps are labeled conceptual.
All layers retain citations, avoid unsupported widget controls and reopen from a source-versioned cache.
issues.verification: Review matched student/technical explanations for two source families; test missing evidence and conflicting explanation fixtures.
issues.evidencePolicy: source-linked interpretation
issues.inferencePolicy: Generate only on explicit request or as part of one bounded import; selecting an already available layer never invokes Meta.

issues.title: Turn supported source equations into manipulable experiments
issues.goal: Change a symbol and see the numerical result and linked visual change beside the unchanged source equation.
issues.scope: Introduce a bounded expression tree for supported arithmetic, vectors and elementary functions, with explicit domains and optional units. Bind an original equation to authored parameter definitions before extending Meta mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: A quadratic example exposes editable coefficients/variables, substitution values and the resulting value and curve.
Every interactive symbol is associated with a definition and a verified mapping to the original equation; ambiguous formulas remain static.
The evaluator rejects arbitrary JavaScript, unsupported operators, invalid units/domains and excessive expression depth.
Keyboard edits, reset, save/share and accessible numerical equivalents preserve the exact expression and parameter values.
issues.verification: Compare supported expressions with independent numerical references; test division by zero, nonfinite values, unit mismatches and malicious input.
issues.evidencePolicy: bounded deterministic computation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Compare the reformatted reader with the original PDF passage
issues.goal: Check an equation, omitted figure or doubtful extraction directly in the original without abandoning the reading flow.
issues.scope: Add a source comparison pane using original local PDF bytes and extraction coordinates where available. Keep the existing separate original link as a fallback and distinguish exact bounding boxes from page/quote references.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a source citation displays the correct original PDF page and preserves the reformatted reader position.
Highlight geometry is shown only when extraction provides a reliable coordinate mapping; otherwise the UI says page/quote only.
Original figures can be inspected as source page regions without presenting generated reconstruction as the original.
The pane is keyboard/touch usable, lazy-loaded, closable and respects local-PDF/bundle permissions.
issues.verification: Check single/two-column pages, equations, missing coordinate maps and local bundles against original PDFs.
issues.evidencePolicy: source rendering
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Declare widget capabilities and controls in one extensible catalog
issues.goal: Add a widget once and make its real interactions discoverable to the renderer, author and Meta planner.
issues.scope: Replace duplicated widget/engine enums and scattered control assumptions with versioned catalog descriptors: data shapes, visual variants, interactions, limits, required evidence, empty states and compatible engines. Deliver usable examples for every descriptor.
acceptanceCriteria: A new widget can be registered without adding its algorithm name to the reader or prompt branches.
Each catalog entry lists actual controls, input bounds, provenance rules, accessible equivalent and a prepared example.
The planner receives only capabilities supported by the active app version; unsupported catalog/version combinations fail explicitly.
Existing graph, array, steps, comparison, matrix and plot snapshots still open under a documented compatibility policy.
issues.verification: Exercise all existing renderers through catalog fixtures and reject unavailable controls, missing fields and stale descriptors.
issues.evidencePolicy: application-owned capabilities
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Add interactive concept diagrams and state-machine walkthroughs
issues.goal: Inspect dependencies, data flow and state changes even when a paper has no executable engine.
issues.scope: Provide bounded node/link diagrams with step-linked highlights, local pan/zoom, selection, optional grouping and textual relationships. Preserve source labels and distinguish authored illustrative transitions from executed traces.
acceptanceCriteria: A source-linked pipeline and a state-machine example each support node selection and step-linked highlighting.
Each edge has a readable meaning and each state has a text description; the diagram remains usable without color or dragging.
An illustrative diagram never displays execution metrics or claims that selected nodes ran an algorithm.
Layout and selected step restore from a validated snapshot with bounded node/link counts.
issues.verification: Review source mappings for two unrelated papers; inspect keyboard navigation, cyclic diagrams, long labels and reduced motion.
issues.evidencePolicy: illustrative unless bound to an existing verified trace
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Make source and computed tables explorable
issues.goal: Inspect rows, variables and tradeoffs instead of reading a static wall of metrics.
issues.scope: Add table selection, bounded filtering/sorting, column definitions and an optional linked bar/dot view. Keep source-reported measurements separate from locally computed results and synthetic teaching data.
acceptanceCriteria: Every dataset declares its origin, units and source reference; source values are never filled in by Meta guesses.
Sorting/filtering changes the view, preserves row identity and does not alter the underlying run or source table.
A selected row or metric can reveal its definition and linked source passage.
An accessible table and CSV/JSON export retain full precision, provenance and visible filtering state.
issues.verification: Compare values with original and engine fixtures; test missing values, mixed units and keyboard-only filtering.
issues.evidencePolicy: explicitly source-reported, computed or illustrative
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Add function plots with draggable probes and linked values
issues.goal: Explore how a mathematical relationship behaves across its domain rather than only watching a residual curve.
issues.scope: Build bounded 1D function/parametric plots from the trusted expression evaluator, with parameter sliders, probes, annotations, optional derivative overlays and explicit discontinuity handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Moving a probe by pointer or keyboard updates the shown x/value and linked equation substitution.
Poles and invalid domains break the plotted curve instead of connecting invalid samples; sampled/interpolated segments are disclosed.
All plotted values derive from an authored expression and recorded parameters, with a numerical table alternative.
Sampling, cancellation, reset and portable snapshots respect fixed budgets and supported evaluator operations.
issues.verification: Check polynomials, sinusoids, discontinuities and boundary values against analytic references; review screen-reader text and narrow layouts.
issues.evidencePolicy: bounded deterministic computation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Make linear algebra visible as geometric transformations
issues.goal: See what matrix entries do to basis vectors, a point and a region.
issues.scope: Start with bounded 2D matrix/vector transformations, bases, projections and conditioning examples. Provide exact numerical values and explicit singular/non-symmetric cases before considering 3D.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing matrix entries or a vector synchronizes the matrix, transformed basis, point and region.
The example distinguishes a singular map, rotation, projection and anisotropic scaling using reference-checked outputs.
Unsupported eigen-decompositions and numerical instabilities have explicit states instead of guessed geometry.
Pointer interactions have keyboard/value alternatives and the full experiment can be reset and restored.
issues.verification: Verify known matrices, determinant/area relationships and transformation composition using independent references and tolerances.
issues.evidencePolicy: bounded deterministic computation; no claim to reproduce all linear algebra in a paper
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Add probability, seeded sampling and Bayesian-update widgets
issues.goal: Build intuition for probability and uncertainty by changing assumptions and observing real samples and updates.
issues.scope: Support a small declared set first: Bernoulli/binomial/normal sampling and a beta-Bernoulli update. Show distribution parameters, observed counts, normalization and exact versus sampled quantities.
acceptanceCriteria: A reader can alter parameters, draw a reproducible seeded sample and compare empirical and analytic quantities.
A beta-Bernoulli example recomputes prior, likelihood and posterior from explicit observation counts.
Density, probability mass, samples and credible intervals are named distinctly with assumptions and units.
Bounds, invalid parameters, RNG version, seeds and observation data are validated and preserved in snapshots.
issues.verification: Check analytic moments, normalization and conjugate updates; use seeded deterministic cases and statistical tests with justified tolerances.
issues.evidencePolicy: analytic deterministic results plus explicitly seeded stochastic samples
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Explain attention through small editable tensor computations
issues.goal: Inspect how query/key scores turn into weights and weighted values for a toy sequence.
issues.scope: Implement only bounded scaled dot-product attention on explicit small Q/K/V matrices. Link score, softmax and output views; introduce toy labels, masks and temperature without pretending to run a trained Transformer.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing an admissible Q/K/V value recomputes dot products, scaled logits, softmax weights and weighted output.
Selecting one query highlights corresponding tensor cells, arithmetic and source equation.
Dimensions, masks, stable softmax, finite values and row normalization are reference-checked; invalid masked rows fail explicitly.
The figure says toy attention computation, shows its synthetic inputs and never claims Transformer training or original paper reproduction.
issues.verification: Compare with an independent small matrix implementation; check extreme logits, all-masked rows, shape errors and source equation mapping.
issues.evidencePolicy: reference-checked small attention mechanism only
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Provide an editable graph and grid algorithm canvas
issues.goal: Construct a counterexample or scenario directly instead of only changing one pre-existing edge weight.
issues.scope: Add node/edge editing, graph layout movement, start/target selection and a bounded grid/obstacle view. Engine capability descriptors decide which operations and semantics each input supports.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can add, delete, connect and move elements with keyboard/value controls as well as pointer interaction.
Invalid graph/grid structure or weights show actionable validation and do not activate an incompatible engine.
Input edits cancel stale execution and reset playback; complete input, layout and selection restore in a snapshot.
At least one graph scenario and one grid scenario expose all assumptions; an unsupported method remains an illustration.
issues.verification: Check constructed graphs against independent distances, unreachable targets, obstacle boundaries and cancellation during editing.
issues.evidencePolicy: computed only through a declared compatible engine; layouts are presentation
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Add signal and image-operator playgrounds
issues.goal: Understand convolution and sampling through a small signal or synthetic image that can be inspected numerically.
issues.scope: Introduce bounded 1D convolution and a small 2D kernel, stepwise products and boundary modes. Add a small frequency representation only with an explicitly verified transform and adequate transfer budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing a kernel or signal updates computed output and highlights the currently multiplied input region.
Boundary handling, stride and normalization are explicit, with hand-checkable impulse/constant examples.
Input/output values have accessible numeric equivalents; any frequency-domain panel reports its sampling convention.
Image inputs are synthetic or explicitly selected local files; changing a kernel uploads nothing and cannot execute generated code.
issues.verification: Compare independent convolution references, impulse responses and border cases; test bounded execution and accessible alternatives.
issues.evidencePolicy: bounded deterministic teaching operators; no inferred private image uploads
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Link source, formula, pseudocode and visual states through semantic events
issues.goal: Selecting a data element or operation explains the same event in every related view.
issues.scope: Introduce typed selection/event channels with stable data identities and revisions. Support linked highlights and source/formula references; replace comparison index alignment only when an engine declares an equivalent semantic event.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a graph node, matrix cell or trace operation updates the relevant visual, formula/pseudocode and source highlights.
Views share one canonical input revision; edits cannot leave a plot showing an older run.
Comparisons use declared semantic checkpoints where meaningful and explicitly independent playback otherwise.
Selections and layout restore without feedback loops, stale highlights or model calls.
issues.verification: Exercise two unrelated families, reordered data, async worker results and incompatible comparison semantics.
issues.evidencePolicy: semantic events must come from source mappings or actual engine traces
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Explore parameter sweeps and stability regions
issues.goal: Compare a range of hypotheses and discover where an algorithm changes behavior.
issues.scope: Add bounded one/two-parameter experiment grids, curve families and small phase diagrams using existing compatible engines. Present the planned run budget and common input/seed policy before execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Every plotted point links to its exact engine version, input, seed, parameter values, status and measured metric.
Sweep cancellation stops queued work; failed/nonconverged cases remain visible rather than becoming interpolated successes.
Comparisons preserve the declared common input/seed policy and units; hardware speedup is not inferred from operation counts.
A selected point reopens its single experiment, and exported results retain provenance and budget settings.
issues.verification: Validate a small grid against independent individual runs; test cancellation, invalid domains, point caps and nonconvergence.
issues.evidencePolicy: actual bounded engine measurements; interpolation is separately labeled
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Compare before-and-after hypotheses with pinned experiment branches
issues.goal: Ask what changes when one assumption or input changes and keep the original result for comparison.
issues.scope: Let the reader pin a baseline, duplicate the experiment, change an admissible assumption and inspect input/output differences. Keep within-source branches local and distinguish causal intervention in a teaching model from a paper claim.
acceptanceCriteria: Pinning records the full source/engine versions, data, seed and parameters of an actual run.
The UI highlights exactly which inputs changed and recomputes each branch independently.
Metric differences require compatible units and completed/partial status labels; changing multiple assumptions remains explicit.
Branches can be reset, exported and reopened without model inference or overwriting the pinned baseline.
issues.verification: Compare known graph and numeric interventions, incomplete runs and incompatible metrics; verify branch restoration.
issues.evidencePolicy: measured differences in declared models, not general causal claims
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Plan diverse widgets from concepts, data and actual capabilities
issues.goal: An imported paper receives the most useful supported views instead of repeated generic step cards.
issues.scope: Separate concept/coverage planning from widget instantiation. Use catalog capabilities, available source data, section purpose and redundancy checks to select widgets and explain placements. Make the plan inspectable and editable.
acceptanceCriteria: Each proposed widget identifies a concept, exact anchor, interaction objective, needed data, provenance and why its type is suitable.
The planner chooses only exposed catalog controls and does not invent data or force an inappropriate computed engine.
A sufficiently supported mixed-concept fixture can receive multiple meaningful widget types; uniform repetition requires an explicit reason.
The user can accept, remove, replace or defer proposals; validation failures are per-widget and preserve successful grounded additions.
issues.verification: Evaluate on a frozen corpus spanning at least five families and missing-data cases; record grounding, usefulness, diversity and unsupported-control failures separately.
issues.evidencePolicy: Meta proposes; application validation and trusted engines own activation and scientific labels
issues.inferencePolicy: Explicit import only, source-versioned plan cache, per-document request/token ceilings and actual usage reporting; no inference on widget interaction.

issues.title: Repair or replace one widget without reanalyzing the whole paper
issues.goal: Fix a poor explanation or unsuitable visual at the point of use while retaining the rest of the paper.
issues.scope: Add targeted feedback, rejected-proposal diagnostics and explicit regenerate/replace actions for one anchored widget. Cache accepted revisions and preserve the last valid version until replacement passes validation.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can report an irrelevant explanation, wrong mapping or unsupported interaction against a particular widget.
A repair submits only the bounded required source context, catalog capabilities and user feedback, with no hidden recursive retries.
Source grounding and capability validation run again; rejection retains the previous valid figure and shows the reason.
Accepted revisions have visible provenance/version history and allow a local undo.
issues.verification: Use malformed repairs, unchanged duplicates, citation drift and provider failures; verify one repair cannot replace other figures.
issues.evidencePolicy: new generated interpretation with the same independent execution/citation guards
issues.inferencePolicy: One explicit paid action per repair attempt, deduplicated and quota-accounted; no automatic paid retry loop.

issues.title: Edit widget settings with constrained natural-language proposals
issues.goal: Say show a simpler input or compare this setting and review a concrete safe change.
issues.scope: Allow Meta to propose a typed catalog patch for the selected widget and current context. Preview changed data, controls and assumptions before applying; arbitrary code/SVG/HTML execution remains excluded.
acceptanceCriteria: A supported request produces a reviewable structured diff describing every changed field and whether recomputation is required.
Only catalog-allowed, bounded settings can change; source text, evidence labels and engine implementations cannot be patched by the model.
Unsupported requests explain the missing capability without executing a substitute or silently granting higher fidelity.
Applying, rejecting and undoing the proposal are explicit, and the last valid snapshot remains recoverable.
issues.verification: Test malicious code-like requests, field injection, incompatible engine changes, ambiguous requests and rejected diffs.
issues.evidencePolicy: validated data/configuration proposals only; no generated executable code
issues.inferencePolicy: Explicit bounded request only; preview/apply/reject do not call Meta again.

issues.title: Enrich long papers through visible, budgeted section coverage
issues.goal: Read and selectively enrich a paper that exceeds one model context instead of being stopped by the current 70,000-character limit.
issues.scope: Keep the full source intact, build a structural map and request enrichment for selected sections with needed neighboring context. Display coverage and costs; reuse a document-wide concept map only when within the declared budget.
acceptanceCriteria: A source larger than the current limit remains intact and can receive grounded widgets for selected sections.
The UI shows analyzed, unanalyzed, failed and unsupported sections; an excerpt is never called complete-paper analysis.
Every request has bounded context, explicit section identities and provenance, and shares a per-document request/token reservation budget.
Cancellation/reload resumes accepted jobs and coverage state without submitting duplicate paid section requests.
issues.verification: Use the existing 47-page held-out failure, duplicated section labels, cross-section definitions and interrupted multi-section work; preserve original baseline scores.
issues.evidencePolicy: grounded partial coverage with explicit incompleteness; no silent truncation
issues.inferencePolicy: Plan and disclose bounded section requests, require explicit selected enrichment, reserve shared quotas and per-document budgets before new work; cache by section/source/catalog version.

issues.title: Evaluate understanding and widget usefulness with real readers
issues.goal: Find whether the richer reader helps people explain a mechanism and answer a concrete question.
issues.scope: Run a small consented formative evaluation with 3–5 students/engineers, defined source-only versus augmented tasks, observed confusion and a frozen varied-paper corpus. Treat recruitment and participant time as external uncertainty.
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks, expected answers, counterbalancing/order limits and success criteria are written before sessions.
Reported participant counts and observations correspond to real sessions; self-review is identified separately if recruitment fails.
Track wrong interpretations, time to find evidence, interaction usefulness and source-return failures without claiming causal learning gains from a tiny study.
Turn observed severe defects into linked issues and retain unsuccessful automatic widget proposals in the scorecard.
issues.verification: Review de-identified task notes and before/after defect dispositions; no fake participant data or automatically sent recruitment messages.
issues.evidencePolicy: observed formative evidence, not a statistical effectiveness claim
issues.inferencePolicy: Reuse cached analyses during sessions where possible; any additional paid test run is explicit and measured.
issues.remaining: Run 3–5 consented real sessions; owner confirmed no participants available.

issues.title: Keep anchored highlights, questions and personal notes
issues.goal: Record a doubt or insight and return to its exact source/experiment later.
issues.scope: Add local highlights and notes anchored to source version, selected quote and optional experiment snapshot. Include user-created tags and explicit export/import with permissions distinct from paper content.
acceptanceCriteria: Create, edit, find and delete notes by keyboard or pointer without changing the original source.
Notes keep stable quote/context anchors and an unresolved state when the source version no longer matches.
An experiment-linked note restores the compatible input and selection or explains missing/incompatible state.
Exports disclose whether source text/PDF is included; no note or local paper is automatically sent to a server.
issues.verification: Test repeated quotes, source-version changes, deletion, bundle round trips and cleared browser storage.
issues.evidencePolicy: personal annotation, never source-author text
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Export a readable paper-and-experiments study pack
issues.goal: Share or print a coherent explanation with actual figure states and all relevant source attribution.
issues.scope: Add a clean print/export view and self-contained bounded study pack containing permitted selected source passages, static figure captures, exact input/parameters, evidence labels and links to reopen experiments.
acceptanceCriteria: The export preview makes source inclusion, notes, original PDF inclusion and author rights explicit.
Static captures retain visible values, assumptions, current step versus final totals, source references and scientific labels.
Print output avoids clipped equations/figures and tiny control labels, and provides a text equivalent of visual-only states.
No signing/session/deletion/provider capability or runtime secret appears in the pack; interactive reopening validates compatibility.
issues.verification: Inspect a real multi-family export in print and another clean browser; scan the exported payload for private capabilities and compare numerical values.
issues.evidencePolicy: captured actual or explicitly illustrative states, not fresh invented results
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Search the local library by passage, concept and annotation
issues.goal: Find a definition or remembered experiment across imported papers without uploading the library.
issues.scope: Create a bounded worker-backed full-text index over locally stored source, user tags and notes, with source-aware results and graceful missing/deleted-source handling. Start without embeddings or cloud discovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Search returns matching source passages, paper titles, definitions and notes with readable snippets and source-version IDs.
Opening a result restores the exact anchor and does not start inference.
Import/removal/version changes update the local index and deletion removes corresponding indexed text.
Indexing is cancellable and resource-bounded; large or unavailable storage produces an actionable state without blocking reading.
issues.verification: Test repeated terms across sources, Unicode/math text, deletion, storage failures and a large saved library.
issues.evidencePolicy: local indexed source/user text, not generated external search results
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Let readers author source-linked widgets without writing code
issues.goal: Turn a useful static passage into a configured interactive figure even when automatic enrichment chooses badly.
issues.scope: Build a catalog-driven composer: select a source anchor, choose an admissible widget, supply explicit teaching data/controls and preview validated output. Keep authored additions and source claims distinct.
acceptanceCriteria: A reader can create and edit a diagram and a computed widget from the catalog without editing source code.
The preview exposes missing inputs, invalid domains, unsupported engines and exact available interactions before saving.
Authorship, source anchor, data origin and evidence class stay visible and portable.
The same validators protect authored, generated and imported figures; the composer cannot grant verification labels or execute arbitrary code.
issues.verification: Follow the workflow in a clean browser, round-trip the authored additions and reject malformed source/data/binding cases.
issues.evidencePolicy: user-authored figures; computed status only through trusted bindings
issues.inferencePolicy: Manual authoring is provider-free; a separate optional Meta suggestion action is explicit and budgeted.

issues.title: Reconstruct paragraphs, headings and equations with inspectable provenance
issues.goal: Make an imported scientific paper pleasant to read while retaining a route to every uncertain original fragment.
issues.scope: Extend source-v2 beyond column order: conservative paragraph joining, line-break/dehyphenation rules, heading detection and equation/caption regions. Preserve raw fragments, confidence and mappings; mathematical transcription requires review.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixed diverse PDF corpus shows measured improvements in paragraph continuity and section navigation against reviewed references.
Raw extracted text and original coordinates remain available; uncertain joins/structure are disclosed instead of silently overwritten.
Equation images/regions remain accessible when semantic math cannot be recovered; generated TeX is not treated as original text without review.
Normalizer version changes invalidate incompatible caches explicitly and do not alter saved older source records in place.
issues.verification: Compare physical pages with normalized output for multi-column layouts, ligatures, hyphenated words, equation-heavy pages and captions; retain regressions and unsupported scans.
issues.evidencePolicy: source reconstruction with provenance and disclosed uncertainty; OCR stays outside this tranche
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Version the richer widget catalog and preserve existing experiments
issues.goal: Upgrade without losing saved papers, old graphs or the work produced by the first release.
issues.scope: Define additive versus breaking catalog/source/snapshot changes, explicit migration boundaries, compatibility diagnostics and local rollback/backup for schema upgrades. Use versioned prepared fixtures rather than silent assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: All release-1.1.0 prepared graph/array/steps/matrix snapshots have explicit open/reject/migrate outcomes.
Unknown widgets and future versions leave source reading and export recovery available.
Migrations preserve source identity, provenance, scientific labels and actual numerical results or disclose why recomputation is needed.
Failed migrations retain the original stored record and do not trigger model analysis.
issues.verification: Run a frozen cross-version fixture suite, interrupted migration/reload and corrupt/unsupported bundle cases.
issues.evidencePolicy: compatibility preservation, never automatic fidelity promotion
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Verify the final Railway workflow and release handoff
issues.goal: Trust that the richer reader, background jobs and sharing behave on the actual private hosted runtime.
issues.scope: At final release only, adapt hosted checks to the Railway Node service: source/worker assets, questions, accepted-job resume/cancel, disabled inference, durable SQLite quotas on its volume, short-link deletion and authorized access. Use deterministic provider stubs for routine CI and bounded real checks separately. Existing Sites/D1 smoke evidence does not verify Railway.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented hosted smoke covers start/retrieve/cancel/question ownership and one reload recovery without duplicated creation.
Routine CI uses provider stubs and no secrets; an explicit authorized real-provider check reports actual requests/tokens separately.
Private audience checks, Railway-volume/SQLite failure behavior, expiry and deletion are tested on the actual release origin without weakening access controls.
Release notes identify exact source commit, artifact, environment revision and remaining manual submission constraints.
issues.verification: Run the hosted suite on a staging/test context and the minimal authorized production checks; retain redacted evidence and fail the release gate on unresolved regressions.
issues.evidencePolicy: actual runtime evidence, distinct from local fixtures and provider stubs

issues.title: Keep rich papers responsive and accessible as widgets grow
issues.goal: Scroll, select text and open a figure smoothly in a long augmented paper.
issues.scope: Measure cold reading, deferred figure mounting, worker transfer and rendering costs on declared fixtures/devices. Lazy-mount heavy visuals with stable placeholders, preserve anchors/search and add focused visual/a11y regression coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: A frozen long-paper fixture reports main-thread responsiveness, worker transfer size and layout shifts before/after optimization.
Offscreen heavy widgets defer expensive work without losing source text, keyboard reachability or find-in-page behavior.
Opening a deferred figure and restoring its snapshot does not jump the reading position or reuse stale data.
Reduced motion, 320 px layouts, 200% zoom and core keyboard paths pass for each new widget family; no universal 60fps claim is made.
issues.verification: Profile actual browser runs with recorded hardware/viewport conditions and a declared regression budget; review representative screenshots and accessible equivalents.
issues.evidencePolicy: measured app responsiveness; no comparison to paper hardware timings
issues.inferencePolicy: No inference for reading, interaction, parameter edits or playback.

issues.title: Prepare the final Railway deployment from the existing Node container
issues.goal: Serve the final application on Railway without rebuilding the frontend or porting the Sites Worker adapter.
issues.scope: At release time, prepare the existing Docker/Next standalone target for Railway: runtime PORT binding, /api/health readiness, pinned build, server-only variables, exact origin and a persistent /data mount. Keep one instance initially; resolve the existing USER node versus mounted-volume ownership before enabling writes.
acceptanceCriteria: The released revision builds and starts on Railway, honors its runtime PORT and serves HTML, PDF worker, engine worker and prepared source assets.
A persistent /data mount is writable by the intended runtime identity; permission handling is explicitly reviewed and tested rather than assumed from image-time chown.
MODEL_API_KEY and stable signing secrets exist only as runtime variables, ANALYSIS_APP_ORIGIN matches the final HTTPS origin, and the initial deployment has new inference disabled.
No Sites-specific static export or D1 binding is required by this Node deployment; the existing private Site remains untouched unless separately requested.
issues.verification: At final release only: verify on the actual Railway service, retain redacted evidence, and record exact source revision, environment and remaining limitations. No provisioning, domain change or paid inference is needed to plan this issue.
issues.evidencePolicy: actual Railway runtime evidence required; existing Sites/D1 and local Docker checks are historical evidence only
issues.inferencePolicy: No paid calls while preparing the release plan. Start with inference disabled; any bounded real Meta smoke at release is explicit and quota-accounted.

issues.title: Verify Railway persistence, access and operating limits before release
issues.goal: Keep quotas and shared links durable and make the final deployment accessible to the intended audience without unexpected exposure or spend.
issues.scope: At release, configure SQLite quota/short-link paths on the mounted volume, test restart/redeploy and backup restoration, confirm the actual Railway plan/resource allowances, document a conservative operating budget and select explicit access controls. Existing Sites authentication does not automatically protect a Railway URL. Multi-instance storage is a separate later decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Quota reservations, short links and deletion/expiry state survive restart and redeploy on the actual mounted storage; a missing or unwritable store fails closed before paid work.
A backup/restore drill is recorded, including how quota history and deleted/expired links are handled; the release runbook records volume-backed redeployment downtime limits.
The chosen Railway plan, limits and operator alerts are reviewed at release without assuming Meta credits cover hosting or that an application token quota is a billing cap.
Private access remains the current requirement; verify intended-reader/judge access and unauthorized-user denial before sharing the URL. Any future public exposure requires an explicit user decision.

readingReferences.title: W3C WCAG 2.2 — Text Spacing (AA)
readingReferences.application: Check that reader content survives user spacing overrides; this does not prescribe the application default.

readingReferences.title: W3C — Visual Presentation (AAA)
readingReferences.application: Use adjustable measure and presentation as design guidance; do not label the current app AAA conformant.

readingReferences.title: Bret Victor — Explorable Explanations
readingReferences.application: Prefer interventions in explicit models and low-friction context beside the text; this is a design direction, not a measured learning result.

readingReferences.title: Olah and Carter — Research Debt
readingReferences.application: Treat explanation quality and notation as substantive product work, with real-reader validation.

readingReferences.title: Railway — Healthchecks
readingReferences.application: Recheck runtime PORT/readiness and volume-backed deployment interruption at release.

readingReferences.title: Railway — Volumes
readingReferences.application: Recheck runtime mount availability and non-root permission handling before configuring /data.

readingReferences.title: Railway — Volume limits
readingReferences.application: The initial proposal is one volume-backed instance, not replicas sharing SQLite.

readingReferences.title: Railway — Volume backups
readingReferences.application: Plan a real backup/restore drill at release; do not claim it has occurred.

deliverySlices.title: A — Comfortable reading
deliverySlices.outcome: A quiet, configurable reader with reliable source navigation.

deliverySlices.title: B — One idea becomes explorable
deliverySlices.outcome: Symbols, one manipulable equation, concept diagrams and function plots on real source passages, with compatible snapshots.

deliverySlices.title: C — Useful automatic enrichment
deliverySlices.outcome: Linked views and budgeted per-section plans, targeted repair and actual reader observations.

deliverySlices.title: D — Breadth and personal workflow
deliverySlices.outcome: Add remaining families and authoring/library tools incrementally after demonstrated usefulness.

deliverySlices.title: E — Final Railway release
deliverySlices.outcome: Only at release time: provision Railway, verify durable storage and access, then smoke-test the actual release origin.

definitionOfDone: A visible, source-linked user interaction works end to end in a real browser.
A computation has independent references and explicit bounds; a concept illustration does not invent execution.
Keyboard, reduced motion, readable values, narrow layout and source return work.
Portable state has validated compatibility and provenance; no private paper is silently uploaded.
Meta calls are explicit, cached and quota-accounted; local interaction is provider-free.
The issue closes only with actual evidence and known limits, not a screenshot or a model assertion alone.
